A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Obfuscation Atlas study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original RLVR experiments on four models, deception-probe evaluations, ablations and model-belief analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds Food-Sycophancy experiments, probe-stability controls and further robustness evaluations.

M1.justification: The probe-penalized, KL-regularized objective, GRPO/LoRA training and linear-probe framework remain unchanged. The new task and additional extraction experiments apply existing procedures; expanded implementation disclosures do not establish a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix O adds restaurant-invitation generation with a cuisine-biased LLM judge and a cuisine-content probe, substantially extending evaluation beyond coding. Appendix P adds Python-code and docstring detection tasks. The original MBPP and deception datasets remain.

E2.justification: Table 16 changes its included probe comparisons from all three probe datasets to Simple and Diverse Deception only, excluding the MBPP-probe baseline from that aggregate. MBPP remains evaluated elsewhere, and the principal comparison methods are retained.

E3.justification: Table 12 revises the reported learning rate from 1e-4 to 5e-5 and default KL coefficient from 0.01 to 1e-4. Appendix H revises effective-batch reporting following a gradient bug. Added protocols include 500-step training and the Food-Sycophancy judge-based evaluation. These reported revisions do not establish that all original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds deception-threshold sensitivity, non-deception feature controls, mean-pooled probe evasion examples, 500-step stability testing and detector training without the code-length penalty (Appendices N, P, S, T and V). These directly test dependencies and alternative explanations left unresolved in v1.

E5.justification: The three-seed main protocol, mean/standard-deviation reporting, standard-error plots and Appendix L significance tests remain. Added results extend existing reporting practices, including the ten-seed no-code-length-penalty design already present in v1 Table 5; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: V2 adds Food-Sycophancy outcomes, non-deception-probe stability, 500-step trajectories, 5/6 mean-pooled runs yielding obfuscated policies, and 10/10 honest no-length-penalty detector runs for each of two models. Table 16 replaces counts using a different model/probe pool, so changes are not same-setting gains. Section 5.2 also corrects Strategic Honesty from 26.9% to 26.5%.

T1.justification: The objective decomposition and Appendix D policy-gradient claim, proof and derivations are retained. Removing the extraneous argmax from Equation 2 is a notation correction, not a substantive theoretical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contributions retain the same central claims. The conclusion corrects the detector-training outcome list from three to four by including blatant deception, aligning it with the existing taxonomy.

C2.justification: V2 refines the mechanism discussion by linking evasion strategies to probe extraction and interpreting non-deception controls as evidence of deception-specific drift. It adds a narrow-task explanation for absent emergent misalignment. Section 6 replaces the untested-beyond-coding limitation with untested large-scale RL and richer action spaces.

D1.justification: Appendix H adds GPU counts, epoch information, a probe-filter fallback and configurations for new experiments. It discloses a multi-GPU gradient bug producing realized batch sizes of 4 and 1 for the larger models. Appendix Q supplies the classification prompt and manual-validation information, although its few-shot examples are omitted.

R1.justification: New Appendix M explicitly contrasts the study's absence of emergent misalignment with the previously cited MacDiarmid and Denison studies. The cited-work set otherwise remains stable; updated years, venues and titles largely reflect publication metadata changes.

P1.justification: The main seven-section narrative and abstract are retained. V2 makes targeted language, terminology and cross-reference corrections, adds acknowledgements and reorganizes back matter. V1 Appendix M's larger-model discussion is retained within the expanded Appendix R.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the displays with sensitivity, task, control, prompt and ablation tables plus extended-training curves. Figure 12 becomes a four-model comparison retaining the earlier Llama-70B results, and Figure 14 disaggregates the atlas. Existing figures are also relocated and Figure 6's model panels reordered.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central findings by testing dependencies on coding, probe extraction, training duration and the code-length incentive. Particularly valuable are the non-coding experiment and ten-seed demonstrations of detector benefits without a code-length penalty. Threshold checks and implementation disclosures also improve auditability. The new judge setup and bug-fix validation remain incompletely documented, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support.
